Application Materials.content:
For the application, applicants should gather supporting documents, including:
- Transcripts and certificates of any essential qualifications.
- Referee details.
- A personal statement, if applicable to the chosen course.
**If you have completed your qualification, you should upload your degree award certificate and degree transcript. If you have not yet completed your degree, please upload your transcript to show results to date.**
For **International Applicants**, Queen’s states that applicants must scan and upload the following supporting documents along with the application:
- Degree transcripts for all completed periods of study, undergraduate level and above.
- If the degree is still in progress, a transcript of results achieved to date.
- Copies of official Degree/Diploma Certificates for completed qualifications.
- Certified translations if original documents are not in English; if translations are not available at application, forward them by email to [student@qub.ac.uk](mailto:intl.student@qub.ac.uk) when available.
- Applicants whose first language is not English will need to show evidence of an acceptable level of competency in the English language.
For references: for all Postgraduate Taught and Research applications, applicants must include the names and contact details of **two referees**, normally academics familiar with undergraduate and/or postgraduate studies. If the applicant has taken a higher degree or postgraduate course recently, one referee should be from that institution. If the applicant has been away from higher education for some time, an employer may be used as one referee. Applicants do **not** need to include reference letters with the application; these will be requested directly by the University if required.

Application Deadlines.content: Applicants are advised to apply as early as possible and ideally no later than **14th August 2026** for courses which commence in **late September**. In the event that any programme receives a high number of applications, the University reserves the right to close the application portal prior to the deadline stated on Course Finder.

Academic Requirements.content:
- **A 2.2 Honours degree in Accounting and/or Finance** or equivalent qualification acceptable to the University; or
- **A 2.2 Honours degree** or equivalent qualification acceptable to the University in **Economics or Mathematics** with **a minimum of two relevant subjects from the core accounting subject list** at a pass mark or international equivalent; or
- **A 2.2 Honours degree** or equivalent qualification acceptable to the University in **Business, Commerce, Management, Law, or any other discipline** with **a minimum of five relevant subjects** at a pass mark or international equivalent. **At least two of these five must be from the core accounting subjects.**
- Accepted subjects: Core accounting subjects include Financial Accounting/Financial Reporting, Management/Cost Accounting, Finance/Financial Management, Auditing, Introduction to Accounting, Principles of Accounting, Advanced Accounting, Accounting Fundamentals, Corporate Accounting, Practical Accounting, Accounting for Managerial Decisions. Other relevant subjects include Investment Analysis, Investment Management, Micro Economics, Macro Economics, Statistics, Mathematics, Mathematical Statistics, Financial Services, Financial Analysis, Financial Markets and Operations, Financial Services.
- For applicants from China Mainland: applicants should hold **a good four-year bachelor degree from a recognised, well ranked university with an average grade of at least 70–85%**. For a **UK 2.2 Hons standard**, the China Mainland thresholds are: Tier 1 **Final average 70%**; Tier 2 **Final average 75%**; Tier 3 **Final average 80%**.
- China Mainland institution tiers: **Tier 1:** Prestigious Universities (Double First Class Universities and Top 100 Academic Ranking of World Universities). **Tier 2:** Other Recognised Universities and Independent Colleges affiliated to a Tier 1 Institution (as defined by Queen's). **Tier 3:** Other Independent Colleges recognised by Ministry of Education and Self-Study Degrees.
- Borderline cases for China Mainland applicants: where entry requirements are different, borderline cases will be considered at the discretion of the Academic Selector; flexibility may be possible for applicants who have fallen more than 2% below the target grade when final results are known, at the discretion of the Academic Selector.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
Evidence of an **IELTS** score of **6.5**, with **not less than 5.5 in any component**, or an equivalent qualification acceptable to the University is required. IELTS must be **taken within the last 2 years**.
International students wishing to apply to Queen's University Belfast, and for whom English is not their first language, must be able to demonstrate their proficiency in English. Non-EEA nationals must also satisfy UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) immigration requirements for English language for visa purposes. More information: [www.qub.ac.uk/EnglishLanguageReqs](https://www.qub.ac.uk/EnglishLanguageReqs).
If you need to improve your English language skills before entering this degree programme, [Queen's University Belfast International Study Centre](https://qubisc.com/en?utm_source=Queens_referral&utm_medium=website_content&utm_campaign=courses/postgraduate-taught/accounting-finance-analytics-msc/&utm_term=INTO+Queen%27s+University+Belfast) offers English language courses, including [Academic English](https://qubisc.com/en/courses/academic-english?utm_source=Queens_referral&utm_medium=website_content&utm_campaign=courses/postgraduate-taught/accounting-finance-analytics-msc/&utm_term=Academic+English) and [Pre-sessional English](https://qubisc.com/en/courses/pre-sessional-english?utm_source=Queens_referral&utm_medium=website_content&utm_campaign=courses/postgraduate-taught/accounting-finance-analytics-msc/&utm_term=Pre-sessional+English).

Program Overview.content:
MSc Accounting, Finance and Analytics at Queen's Business School is a 1 year full-time postgraduate taught programme. The course was previously known as MSc Accounting and Finance. It combines data analytics with accounting and finance, and is designed for a data-driven business environment where accounting and financial decisions are supported by accurate data analysis, predictive models, and strategic insights.
The programme provides:
- Market-leading professional exemptions from the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA), Chartered Institute of Management Accounting/American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (CIMA/AICPA), and Chartered Accountants Ireland (CAI).
- Enhanced employability through hands-on engagement with profession-relevant analytics tools and technologies, in a programme developed and delivered with employers.
- A supportive student experience with high quality teaching and active engagement with contemporary research.
The MSc Accounting, Finance and Analytics offers substantial exemptions from ACCA professional examinations, including Business and Technology (BT), Management Accounting (MA), Financial Accounting (FA), Corporate and Business Law (LW), Audit and Assurance (AA), Financial Management (FM), Financial Reporting (FR), and Performance Management (PM). It offers full exemption from AICPA/CIMA's Certificate and Operational levels, entering at the Management Level Case Study entry point, with further exemptions available from E2, P2 and F2. It also offers partial exemption from CAI's CAP1 level, providing exemptions from Finance and Management Accounting examinations.
The programme has been developed with employers and includes employer engagement across its modules, including real life simulations in Business Games, assessment, guest lectures and masterclasses. It also includes a Queen's Business School Employability module running throughout the programme.
The programme blends Accounting, Finance, and Analytics. Students gain understanding of financial principles and accounting frameworks while developing advanced data analysis skills. Students learn how to analyse, interpret, and leverage data to make financial forecasts, assess risks, and identify opportunities, using software such as Stata, Excel, PowerBI, Matlab, Python, R and databases such as WRDS, Thomson One Banker, DataStream and Bloomberg.
The programme offers advanced study in accounting, finance and analytics, preparing students for careers in financial institutions, management consulting, industry, the public sector, or PhD study in accounting and finance. In the third semester, students choose either a traditional Dissertation or Audit, Ethics and Capstone Project. The capstone route combines taught classes with additional professional exemptions and a final capstone project requiring data analysis and delivery of a professional-quality report and presentation, including visualisations, to a professional audience of employer representatives.
Students have access to the Queen's Business School building beside Riddel Hall, including a 250-seat tiered lecture space, a 120-seat Harvard-style theatre, a 150-seat computer laboratory, the FinTrU Trading Room, breakout study areas, a cafe, and a Business Engagement and Employability Hub. Students also have access to Bloomberg terminals in the FinTrU Trading Room.
A dedicated team of Queen's Business School Postgraduate Student Advisers offers support including English language assistance, study skills classes, academic skills development, time and project management, and guidance on referencing and citation.
People teaching on the programme include Dr Bibek Bhatta, Senior Lecturer and Programme Director, whose research spans energy policy, finance, and climate with a focus on Big Data; Dr Enayet Karim, Lecturer in Accounting, whose research focuses on textual analysis of corporate reports, auditing, risk disclosure, sustainability, and behavioural accounting; Dr Mohamed Elsayed, Senior Lecturer in Accounting, whose research interests include market-based accounting research, corporate governance, corporate disclosures, corporate failure, textual analysis, and external auditing/internal controls; Dr Xinwu He, Lecturer in Accounting, whose research interests include Sustainability Reporting, Integrated Reporting and Corporate Social Responsibility; Ms Brenda Clerkin, Senior Lecturer of Practice (Accounting), who teaches auditing, ethics, data analytics and modern technologies; Professor Danielle McConville, Professor in Accounting and Head of Department for Accounting at QBS, whose teaching specialisms include accounting information systems, contemporary technologies and management accounting; and Professor Martin Quinn, Professor in Accounting, whose teaching area is management accounting and whose research focuses on organisational and accounting change.
This Masters programme provides the basis for both profession- and research-orientated careers, as well as skills and knowledge required to progress into management careers in accounting and financial services. It opens career opportunities in banking, accounting and auditing, government, corporate finance, investment analysis and academia. Queen's is ranked third in the UK for Graduate Prospects in Accounting and Finance (Times and Sunday Times Good University Guide 2024). Graduates from the programme's predecessor, MSc Accounting and Finance, have secured roles with employers such as Bank of China, Deloitte, EY, KPMG, PwC, Allstate, and many others. Typical graduate roles include chartered and certified accountants, consultants, auditors and finance professionals.
Course location: Queen's Business School.

Curriculum.content:
Attendance: **1 year (Full-time)**.
Course Structure: The programme offers the opportunity to pursue appropriately advanced studies in accounting, finance and analytics. In the first semester, students take four modules; in the second semester, students take an additional four modules; in the third semester, students choose either a traditional Dissertation or Audit, Ethics and Capstone Project.
- **Semester 1 (60 CATS):** International Financial Accounting and Reporting; Contemporary Research Methods and Analysis; Corporate Finance; Business Technologies and Analytics.
- **Semester 2 (60 CATS):** Management Accounting for Decision Makers; Accounting for Sustainability; Advanced Business Technologies and Analytics; Money and Banking OR International Finance (Choose one).
- **Semester 3 (60 CATS):** Route 1 – Dissertation OR Route 2 – Audit, Ethics and Capstone Project.
Core Modules:
- Dissertation – MSc Accounting Finance & Analytics (**60 credits**)
- International Financial Accounting and Reporting (**15 credits**)
- Contemporary Research Methods and Analysis (**15 credits**)
- Management Accounting for Decision Makers (**15 credits**)
- Corporate Finance (**15 credits**)
- Audit, Ethics and Capstone Project (**60 credits**)
- Business Technologies and Analytics (**15 credits**)
- Accounting for Sustainability (**15 credits**)
- Advanced Business Technologies and Analytics (**15 credits**)
Optional Modules:
- International Finance (**15 credits**)
- Money and Banking (**15 credits**)
Route 1 – Dissertation: The aim of the dissertation is to provide students with the skills needed for conducting theoretical and/or empirical research in accounting and finance.
Route 2 – Audit, Ethics and Capstone Project: This route combines taught classes with additional professional exemptions and a final capstone project. Auditing and Accountability is 25%, Ethics and Governance is 25%, and Capstone Project is 50%. The Capstone Project requires data analysis plus delivery of a professional-quality report and presentation, including visualisations, to a professional audience comprised of employer representatives.

Financial Aid.content:
Four Vice Chancellor’s International Attainment Scholarships - Postgraduate Taught offer a **50% reduction on full tuition fees** to exceptionally talented international students paying international tuition fee rates who will be starting full-time postgraduate taught studies in 2026/27 on an eligible programme, including **MSc Accounting, Finance and Analytics**. The 50% tuition fee reduction is paid for all years of the programme, up to a **maximum of two years**.
Applicants can only apply and be considered after they have been offered a place on their chosen eligible programme and have **FIRMLY** accepted their offer. The offer **must be confirmed** as the applicant’s FIRM choice by the scholarship deadline. Applications close **Thursday 7 May 2026 15:00 BST**.
To apply, applicants must submit a short video and complete the online application form. The video topic is: **Why you want to come and study at Queen's University Belfast and how you believe your programme of choice will benefit you in your future career aspirations.** Videos that exceed **2 minutes** will not be considered, and videos received after **15:00 BST Thursday 7 May 2026** will not be opened.
Eligibility and conditions include:
- Students must hold an offer of a full-time place at Queen’s University Belfast campus for 2026/27 on one of the specified postgraduate taught programmes, including **MSc Accounting, Finance and Analytics**.
- Students must be classified as international fee-paying students paying the full international tuition fee rate. Students paying NI ROI, EU or GB fees are not eligible.
- Students must be self-funded, i.e. paying the tuition fees for the course themselves at the international rate.
- If a student is in receipt of funding, either tuition fees or tuition fees and living costs, from an external sponsorship body such as Government, a charity or a private organisation, they will not be eligible. This excludes students in receipt of educational loans.
- Applicants may apply and/or be considered for more than one tuition fee award administered by Queen’s University Belfast, but if successful would receive **only** the highest value award.
- The Vice Chancellor’s International Attainment Scholarship - Postgraduate Taught may be combined with the Early Confirmation Award or ISC Scholarship where eligible.
- The University is unable to consider requests for increased and/or further funding; the amount of scholarship offered is non-negotiable.

Multiple Applications.content:
After you have entered the core details about yourself and your academic background, you can apply for one or multiple courses.
If you have applied for and been offered a place on more than one programme of study, you must indicate whether you wish to accept or decline the offer against each programme. Given that your final programme choice may be dependent on funding and/or other factors, you may initially decide to accept more than one offer of a place.

Deferral Admission Policy.content: Applications for deferred entry may be permitted. However, in considering requests for deferred entry it will be necessary to consider if the course will be offered in a subsequent year or, in the case of research, the research project and/or intended supervisor is available in a subsequent year. Requests will be considered on an individual basis, particularly in relation to non-UK/Irish applicants who may have experienced delays in obtaining an entry visa in time to commence their studies. Applications for deferral of University administered funding are not permitted.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
- To accept or decline an offer, applicants should reply online through the [Queen's Portal](https://go.qub.ac.uk/pgapply), ideally within **14 days from receipt of your offer letter**, even if they have not met the conditions of the offer yet.
- If an offer is conditional upon completion of a degree or other qualification, such as an English language examination, applicants should upload a scanned copy of official examination results through the Queen's Portal.
- Conditional offer holders should upload scanned copies of their **final transcript and degree award certificate**, along with their **English language qualification** if appropriate, to the [Queen's Portal](https://go.qub.ac.uk/pgapply). Where applicable, qualifications must be officially translated into English.
- Applicants should submit results even if they have not exactly met the academic condition(s) of the offer, as Queen's says "it may be possible to exercise some flexibility if places are available."
- Queen's University Belfast International Study Centre offers English Language courses which may assist students to meet the required standard of English language for entry, including [English for University Study](https://qubisc.com/en/courses/academic-english) and [Pre-sessional English](https://qubisc.com/en/search?facet-StudyLevel=%22English%20Language%22&facet-ProgramGroups=%22Pre-sessional%20English%22).
- Pre-sessional English programmes are offered in durations of **6 or 10 weeks**. Start dates are **Mon 15 June 2026-Fri 21 August 2026 (10 weeks)** and **Tues 15 July 2026-Fri 21 August 2026 (6 weeks)**. Academic entry requirement: applicants **must hold an offer of a place on a degree programme at Queen's University Belfast**.
